concerns.text: New yellowing of the whites of the eyes today with brief right-rib aches after greasy food in a 51 year old (with no fever, chills, or continuous severe pain stated) is labelled hospital (level 4), which is plausible for urgent imaging and evaluation of acute common bile duct obstruction, though whether afebrile new scleral icterus with brief postprandial aches requires immediate hospital care rather than a same-day doctor visit (level 2) is a clinician's call.

The control (jaw joint locked rigid wide open when opening the mouth wide in an adult with 4 months of morning sore back teeth and teeth clenching) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for prompt manual reduction of acute anterior mandibular dislocation, though whether an uncomplicated open jaw lock requires emergency department care rather than urgent same-day oral surgery or dentist reduction (level 3) is a clinician's call.

Trying to conceive through regular intercourse for 18 months at ages 28 and 29 is labelled specialist (level 3) past the 12-month infertility threshold, though whether initial fertility evaluation begins with a reproductive/gynecology specialist (level 3) or a general physician ordering baseline labs and semen analysis first (level 2) is a clinician's call.
'Hot boggy swelling across his scalp' in changed_fact uses 'boggy', which leans toward clinical palpation vocabulary rather than everyday parent wording.

The control (hot boggy swelling across the scalp today in a 7 year old boy after 10 days of scalp itching behind both ears with tiny white specks on the hair strands, with no fever or lethargy stated) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for suspected pediatric deep scalp cellulitis or subgaleal abscess, though whether boggy scalp swelling requires emergency department care rather than a same-day pediatric clinic visit (level 2) is a clinician's call.

The control (red streaks spreading up from thick yellow big toes today in a 68 year old, with no fever or systemic symptoms stated) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for acute ascending bacterial lymphangitis in an older adult, though whether early ascending red streaks without stated systemic sepsis require emergency department care rather than a same-day doctor visit (level 2) is a clinician's call.

Having loose motions and mild belly bloating after drinking milk every day for 4 weeks in a 32 year old (with no weight loss, fever, or blood stated) is labelled clinic (level 2) on the 4-week chronic diarrhea threshold, though whether strictly milk-triggered loose stools with mild bloating requires an outpatient clinic visit versus an initial home dairy-avoidance or over-the-counter lactase trial (level 1) is a clinician's call.

The control (sore muscles in the front of the thighs 2 days after a first gym squat workout that make the 25 year old speaker limp on every step, with no focal pop, swelling, or dark urine stated) is labelled doctor/clinic (level 2), which is plausible for evaluating a gait-altering quadriceps strain, though whether peak 48-hour post-squat soreness causing a limp requires a doctor visit rather than initial rest and home self-care (level 1) is a clinician's call.
